subject.title: [Bug]: Mattermost slash commands default to cleartext callback URLs that expose reusable command tokens

question: Should Mattermost native slash-command registration fail closed for any non-HTTPS callback URL, including both derived and explicit HTTP URLs?
rationale: The stricter policy closes cleartext transport for reusable command tokens but intentionally breaks HTTP callback deployments until operators configure HTTPS.

options.title: Require HTTPS before registration
options.body: Land a Mattermost plugin gate that refuses non-HTTPS callbacks before registering native slash commands, with release-note and docs upgrade guidance.

options.title: Stage a compatibility path
options.body: Keep current behavior temporarily while adding a maintainer-approved warning, doctor check, or opt-in strict mode before a later fail-closed release.

options.title: Keep HTTP callbacks allowed
options.body: Accept the cleartext transport risk for operator-controlled networks and close the hardening request without changing registration behavior.

recommendation.title: Require HTTPS before registration
recommendation.body: Land a Mattermost plugin gate that refuses non-HTTPS callbacks before registering native slash commands, with release-note and docs upgrade guidance.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits in the current monitor registration helper that this owner recently refactored, and it needs security/upgrade policy judgment beyond a mechanical patch.
